articles.title: The imperative to prepare for AI-safe data security
articles.content: The proliferation of AI tools in business is redefining the need for data security and trust. As autonomous, decision-making AI agents move from pilot projects into core business workflows, they are expanding the enterprise attack surface just as fast as they are being adopted. Gartner predicts that 40% of enterprise applications will feature task-specific AI agents by the end of 2026, a jump from less than 5% in 2025. Gartner’s advice to leaders of software organizations is to set their agentic AI strategy or “risk being outpaced by the competition”. Security is changing. What was once a “simple” focus on encryption and perimeter defense is no longer enough on its own: the rise of AI-driven risk has transformed it into a multi-dimensional challenge built on algorithmic trust, model integrity, and synthetic data exposure. Trust boundaries are shifting, and most companies aren’t yet equipped to handle it. Yet AI has already been proven unsafe by its very makers, with the Hugging Face breach showing it was a rogue AI agent's fault. The unknown future risk of autonomous agents capable of “emergent” behavior poses huge issues for maintaining security. But this is just one risk of many faced by enterprise cyber security leaders. In fact, the statistics of cyber security investment highlight that business is vastly underprepared for new threats. While the estimated annual cost of cybercrime is $10.5 trillion globally and predicted to reach $15.63 trillion by 2029, this eclipses Gartner’s information security spend prediction of $244 billion in 2026. Machine data is exacerbating the data quality issue with garbage in, garbage out. This calls for technology and trust architectures to be redesigned, with internet security embedded into the data lifecycle. Security leaders will need to make considered investments in AI-safe security, transparency, and federated governance to protect their enterprise ecosystems. The biggest security risks we’re underestimating right now With many threats now AI-driven, it’s unlikely that a single enterprise has protection against all the necessary risks, which is why it’s incumbent on business leaders to prioritize next-level data security. Firstly, polymorphic, AI-generated attacks are hitting bigger and faster, beyond any company’s human ability to counter these attacks. Deepfake is one such AI-powered theft and extortion technique that can be generated in minutes, costing a mere $1,000 (if that) to create a malicious bot that can hack into your system and go after your business’ crown jewel data. Using these methods, hackers can affect AI models by manipulating decision-making itself instead of through direct attacks on the IT infrastructure . Shadow AI and exposure to synthetic data are also growing concerns as employees adopt unsanctioned or non-firewalled AI tools, models and workflows to complete mundane tasks and reporting. Next is the surge in agentic adoption without control of the risk, especially third-party risk, which is huge. Agentic AI has significantly increased the threat surface, with systems capable of autonomously taking actions. In the rush to implement AI, access is being granted for agents to all kinds of data, even to highly sensitive data, often bypassing traditional enterprise controls. All kinds of blind spots emerge when agents are connected to external systems whose security vulnerabilities aren’t vetted. Prompt injections are another critical risk, on a similar level to the whole third-party dependency. It's the idea that an organization doesn’t know what is actually making its way into their system. At first appearing benign, it can build up to turn malicious at some point in time. When it hits, the business won't know what hit them. As if this isn’t enough, we’re counting down to “Q-Day”, when quantum computers become powerful enough to break today’s widely used encryption software standards. This is the stage when attackers will be able to intercept, decrypt, and…

articles.title: Google's search revenue Ferrari hits an AI-powered speed bump
articles.content: Google is paying a higher price for its bet on AI than even Alphabet's $51.4 billion in Q3 capital expenditures suggest. The biz appears to have traded its high-performing search advertising business for the mediocre monetization of AI Overviews and AI Mode, a misstep that contributed to investor concerns as Alphabet lost roughly $500 billion in market value despite management's attempts to reassure Wall Street. Google's year-over-year search revenue growth slowed from 17 percent in Q2 to 12 percent in Q3 . It's still headed in the right direction, but at a slower rate. During Alphabet's conference call for investors, Douglas Anmuth from JPMorgan Chase & Co asked whether that's because Google is showing fewer ads in AI Overviews and AI Mode than it shows in its traditional search results. Chief business officer Philipp Schindler cited several reasons for that: foreign exchange rates, Europe's elimination of its customs-duty exemption, and "the lower monetization we were seeing in AI Mode." To compensate, Google said it is expanding the distribution of AI Overview ads and adding multiturn ads in the US for AI Mode queries. But some Google Ads customers appear to be more concerned about quality than quantity. In a social media post , Max Anderson, CEO of OnlyFinder, complained that Google has responded to declining search volumes by attempting to manufacture revenue growth through "short-sighted, highly extractive, customer-hostile tactics," such as charging advertisers more for lower-quality clicks, including clicks on search terms they had not agreed to target. Eric Seufert, an analyst with Mobile Dev Memo, dismissed the doomsayers in a blog post . "It’s tempting to look at the successive deceleration in Search revenue growth from Q1 2026 as a response to pressure from other chatbots and to assume that Search query volume is migrating elsewhere," he wrote. "But the earnings release notes that the 'year-over-year Search query growth rate [was] the highest it has been in the last five years' in Q3, so it's clear that Search usage isn't declining." So people are still searching, and the business is still growing, but less convincingly, thanks to the lower monetization of AI Overviews and AI Mode. And Google's answer involves more ads in AI interactions. Nate Elliott, principal analyst for AI at Emarketer, told The Register in an email that AI represents a double-edged sword for Google's ad business. "On the one hand, Google owns the thing that people use AI for most: search," Elliott wrote. "Our surveys say that by far the top reason people use AI is to look for facts and information. Luckily for Google, people also tell us they haven't stopped using search engines – they've simply added AI as a new behavior on top of search. That means people spend more time than ever looking for information, and most of those people don't even think twice before doing their searches on Google. If Google figures out how to effectively monetize those users, that's great news for them." But, said Elliott, people may find tools they like better than Google Search as they become accustomed to AI-based discovery. "If ChatGPT or Claude or Muse is better at helping them find what they're looking for, people's search habits might change for the first time in a generation," he said. "That's potentially catastrophic for Google's ad business. The same is true if they maintain their market share but simply can't figure out how to make money from this new kind of discovery. "The problem is, Google isn't giving us very much information about what the specific impact is of AI on their business right now, so everyone's reading into the tiny scraps of information they are releasing." Elliott said it's remarkable that Google has managed to keep the largest and most mature digital ad business growing at a double-digit rate every quarter in recent years. "But it appears that most folks disagree, and instead are concerned that the advertising business 'only' grew…

articles.title: Bought a new tablet for your kids? Here's how to lock it down before handing it over
articles.content: Whether you're worried about your smaller child accidentally clicking through the wrong apps, or maybe an older child that’s a little too curious for their own good, you should know how to secure their new tablet. Here’s how to establish a safe space for your child to use your device. Setting up an Amazon Fire Kids Tablet (Image credit: Future) One of the simplest tablets to set up for your kids is the Amazon Fire Kids Tablet . I’ve used it for my own kid for many years, and while it does have its frustrating quirks, it does get the job done. Bear in mind this is effectively just a Fire Tablet with a colorful case, so it does include an adult profile that is necessary to set up to manage the device. After you’ve created your profile, you’ll create an Amazon Kids Profile. It’ll guide you through a list of settings that you can customize to your child’s needs and send them on their way. In order to monitor and adjust settings on the tablet, go to the Amazon Parent Dashboard (you can do this remotely). From here you can adjust settings like time limits on apps, content filters, and even add content from an adult library. For example, I had to manually add HBO so I could put on Sesame Street . If you do need to lock the device down for any reason, you can hit Pause or Lock Device on the Amazon Parent Dashboard. You can set a duration or set it indefinitely until the device is unlocked by you. Setting up an Android tablet (Image credit: Tom's Guide) For an Android tablet , the first thing you’ll want to do is set up Google Family Link either through a web browser or the app itself on your own device (Android or iOS). From there you can create your child’s account, which includes creating an email address for them (weird, I know). Then when you’re actually setting up the tablet, you can sign in using your child’s email address. It’ll prompt you to sign into your own account afterward. If your child is on the younger side (under 9), you can put them on Google Kids Space , which is tailored with content-restricted apps, books, and YouTube Kids videos. You’ll still have access to parental controls with this app. If Google Kids Space is not for your child, or it’s unavailable for your device, you’ll be able to manage the general kids experience in Google Family Link. Here you can control app approvals and limits, set screen time limits and even set a scheduled bedtime. You can also manage how Google Chrome is used and which sites your child can visit. Locking the device down is as simple as clicking Lock now in the Family Link app. You can use Downtime to run this on a schedule, and you can also use it to grant bonus time. Setting up an iPad (Image credit: Tom's Guide) You can go to your iPad settings, select Family Sharing, Add Member, and create a child account. From there, follow the prompts until the account is created, and set a unique screen time password so your child can’t override the settings. You can configure parental controls from your Apple device or the iPad itself. Navigate back to Family Sharing, click on your child’s name, and then select Screen Time. From here you can adjust content restrictions on apps and websites, even limiting accessible websites to one or two trusted sources. You’ll be able to set time limits and schedules for apps as well, and can also lock them into a single app with Guided Access in the Accessibility settings. Make sure to adjust the Communication settings as well to manage who they can contact. To lock the device, you can access the parental controls remotely and turn on Downtime — this can be immediate or set on a schedule. Bottom line It’s not terribly difficult to set up a new tablet for your kids, although I know from experience that it’s not always seamless. Make sure you look over the parental controls thoroughly. It has less to do with lack of trust and more to do with safeguarding. It’s all too easy for kids to get access to something that they’re not supposed to. I’d also be careful…

articles.title: Samsung’s next foldable is here, and it’s even more expensive than the iPhone Duo
articles.content: Credit: Samsung China TL;DR Samsung has launched the W27 foldable phone in China. This is effectively a Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra with a high-end design. The Samsung W27 starts at ~$2,852 for the 16GB/512GB model. Samsung usually releases China-exclusive variants of its Galaxy Z Fold line each year, complete with swanky designs. The company teased the arrival of the Samsung W27 a few days ago, and it’s now made the device official. The Samsung W27 is indeed a Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra with a more premium design. Expect a gold-colored frame and camera island, while the frame itself now has a textured finish. You can also choose between a dark red or dark blue rear cover. You’re still getting the same Gorilla Glass Ceramic 3 protection on the back, along with that ho-hum IP48 rating . It also has the same 8.9mm folded thickness and 215-gram weight.
articles.author: Hadlee Simons

articles.title: I'm trying the 'burrowcore' trend this fall — here are 3 upgrades to make your home cozier from just $10
articles.content: With the clocks changing and the nights getting darker, I just want to cozy up at home. Dimmed lights, thick, fluffy throws, and a delicious hot chocolate — that’s me set until spring! I’m officially hibernating and creating a warm, snug retreat that looks lived-in and loved, not perfectly polished. Turn your home into a burrow (Image credit: Getty Images) I seem to be unintentionally following the season’s interior trend — Burrowcore. Inspired by storybook animal dens and classic children’s literature, it’s all about creating spaces that feel safe and comforting . “It’s less about creating a perfectly styled space and more about layering warmth, texture and comfort so a room feels lived in and inviting, especially as the evenings get darker,” says Ellie Brown, in-house interior designer at Oak&More . And the best part is that you don’t need a big budget to get the look, with Brown adding, “A few considered changes can completely transform how a room feels.” I don’t know about you, but I’m ready to create my own cold-weather bunker, dim the bright lights and scatter a cozy glow across my living space. Get layering (Image credit: Getty Images) A simple way to create a cocooning feel is to mix different textures, and it’s easy to achieve. “Texture is what makes a space feel snug. Chunky knits, wool, velvet, boucle and linen all add depth and softness, and they work best when you mix a few rather than sticking to just one,” explains Brown. Soft furnishings can help you bring the trend into the room, with Brown saying, “Throws, cushions, rugs and heavier curtains instantly make a room feel warmer.” It’s also easy to swap in a few items to create the look without spending out on redecorating a whole room. In a dining room, Brown suggests placing seat cushions on chairs, a table runner across the table, and a rug underneath, all of which will make the formal area feel more inviting. Whereas in a bedroom, you can add different layers and textures with plain knitted and patterned woolen blankets. Farmhouse Boho Knitted Throw: $19 Create a cozy vibe with this burnt-orange knitted throw, perfect for fall. Use it as a blanket or over your couch to keep the chill out. It features an attractive geometric design and layers well. The throw measures 50 x 60 inches, and it’s machine washable. View Deal Go deeper with earthy tones (Image credit: Shutterstock) Brown says the color palette is just as important as the textures, and fall is the perfect time to go a little deeper. “Burrowcore leans towards rich, enveloping shades such as burnt terracotta, deep moss, warm browns and muted ochre. Darker colors make a room feel more enclosed and cozy, which is exactly the effect you want, especially during the autumnal months,” she says. However, you don’t need to get your paintbrush out to transform your walls, Brown suggest bringing in the deeper, earthy tones with statement pieces and accessories. Votive candle holders: $10 You don't need to spend big to add cozy touches to your home. These two amber glass candle holders have a decorative ribbed design. Turn your lights down and enjoy the ambient glow of tealight candles. View Deal Choose furniture that anchors a room (Image credit: Shutterstock) While soft furnishings create a cozy vibe, furniture grounds the look, and Brown adds that natural materials work particularly well with this trend. “Solid oak has a warmth and character that sits naturally alongside earthy tones and layered textures, so a dining table or sideboard can become the anchor of a room without feeling heavy or overly formal,” she says. I tend to favor an eclectic look and have a mix of pine and oak furniture in my living room; some pieces were bought new and have since been painted to extend their life, while other pieces were bought second-hand from thrift stores. I find this mix of color tones adds warmth. Once you’ve sorted your furniture, Brown adds, “You can then pair it with warm, earthy accessories and your space will…

articles.title: Proton CEO Is In 'Full AI Psychosis'
articles.content: According to 404 Media, Proton CEO Andy Yen is aggressively pushing AI adoption while fostering what workers describe as a culture of fear that discourages raising security concerns or challenging leadership. The investigation is based on interviews with eight current and one former Proton employees, as well as internal Slack chats, meeting recordings, and an AI manifesto written by the company's CTO. Longtime Slashdot reader devnulljapan summarizes the findings: Engineers at Proton, which makes the encrypted email service Proton Mail and a suite of privacy- and security-focused products, including an encrypted drive service, an authenticator app, and a password manager, are being pushed to "stop lovingly handcrafting all our code and use AI more." Workers describe an environment where employees have genuine concerns about security or being asked to develop security products with AI but feel unable to voice them, lest Yen berates them in front of everyone or threatens their employment at the company. "The CEO is in full AI psychosis and has been for a while now," one of the sources told 404 Media. Yen reportedly dismissed an employee's request for additional security testing before releasing new code, calling it "bullshit and loser thinking" and insisting that "only losers think like that." In a separate exchange over Proton's post-quantum encryption rollout, Yen criticized how the company communicated the feature's limitations and told employees that "perception is more important than truth, the truth doesn't matter if you don't win on perception." "The train is coming, get onboard or get crushed. Don't be the professional fax machine operator in the internet age," Yen wrote to the security Slack channel. "I think by the end of this year most developers stop programming and start writing specs for tests that AI will code and run, to validate AI written code that humans will no longer be able to review. This will be the last year that we hire engineers, and starting next year we hire what we used to call product managers, to build things with AI." Read more of this story at Slashdot.

articles.title: Google is giving Gemini’s overlay a literal sparkle on your Android phone
articles.content: TL;DR Google is rolling out a new Gemini overlay animation to all Android phones. The animation uses Google’s Neural Expressive design language and gives Gemini an ethereal look. The redesign is rolling out as part of a Google app update. Google loves redesigning things, and Gemini is one of the things it loves redesigning the most. We’ve already seen the company experiment with new animations for Circle to Search and Gemini Live. We also spotted a new Gemini animation that later arrived on the Pixel 11 series. Well, if you were hoping to get that new Gemini design without buying a new Pixel, you’re in luck. A new Google app update is now finally bringing the updated Gemini design to all Android devices (spotted via 9to5Google ). The redesign brings Google’s Neural Expressive design language to the Gemini overlay, complete with the sparkling effects and tiny dots surrounding the “Ask Gemini” text box.
articles.author: Akshay Gangwar

articles.title: Farm PC 'maintained' by a 14-year-old dumped support chap in a steaming pile of tech mess
articles.content: Welcome to another instalment of On Call, the reader-contributed column The Register publishes each Friday as a cathartic service for readers who know that dealing with tech support BS can be a cow of a job. This week, meet a reader we'll Regomize as "Jason" who told us he had helped an agricultural equipment dealer with his computer issues for about 20 years. "One day this guy called me to ask if I could help at a farm in Yorkshire, where he'd arranged the supply and installation of a fairly substantial system that used a computer to do effectively everything for a few hundred cattle," he told On Call. "That meant individually feeding them, measuring milk yields, planning pregnancies, and periodically submitting all the data to the government." Jason said other tech support folk had tried, and failed, to fix the system. "This had somewhat soured the relationship between the agricultural equipment dealer and the farmer," he punned in his email to On Call. Well punned, Jason. But we digress. "Despite not being fond of wading around in cow shit at four in the morning, I agreed to take a look at the system," Jason told us. By this time he had learned that the farm produced many tons of milk each week, so assumed he would find serious industrial-scale tech once he reached the farm. That assumption was wrong. "When I arrived, the first thing that I found to worry about was that the whole thing was controlled by proprietary software on a single PC running Windows XP – just after Microsoft ended mainstream support." The other things to worry about were all acts of omission: the farm had no backups, no spare PC, and nobody on site to maintain the PC. Jason asked if anyone was responsible for keeping the computer up to date with the security patches and was told the farmer's 14-year-old grandson had done some computer studies at school, so he got the job. That lad had either not discovered, or deleted, the many rather racy videos Jason found on the PC. "When the farmer's wife learned of this, there was what can best be described as a hullabaloo," Jason told On Call. As he dug into the mess, Jason found that the computer was sending milk production data to Her Majesty's Government. He also found that neither the government, nor the farm management software vendor, had bothered to require installation of a firewall. Jason says he installed one, made a few other tweaks, and got the system working. "Everyone seemed pleased, or at least they did until they got my bill," he wrote. "And to be fair, they did pay it promptly." Jason never heard from the farm again. "I don't know if that's because it's still working OK, or if they're just too embarrassed to see me again, or they found someone cheaper who could cope with my recommendations," he wrote. What's the strangest or dirtiest place you've been asked to deliver tech support? Don't cheese us off by holding back! Click here to send us your story so we can milk it for all it's worth in a future instalment of On Call. ®
articles.author: Simon Sharwood

articles.title: New on Peacock in November 2026: All the new shows and movies to watch
articles.content: The holidays are creeping closer, and Peacock’s November 2026 lineup gives streamers plenty to be thankful for. Whether you're settling in for sweeping drama or looking to unwind, this month delivers a balanced mix to carry you through the final stretch of the year. Leading the charge on Nov. 6 is “The Uprising,” a large-scale drama from “Captain Phillips” director Paul Greengrass. Andrew Garfield stars as the leader of a 14th-century English peasant rebellion inspired by the Robin Hood legend. The tension shifts to modern suspense on Nov. 12 with “The Good Daughter,” adapted from Karin Slaughter’s bestseller. The limited series pairs Rose Byrne and Meghann Fahy as estranged sisters forced together when a fresh tragedy reopens their small town’s darkest secrets. Craving something lighter ahead of Thanksgiving? “Dig” drops on Nov. 23, teaming Amy Poehler and “Parks and Recreation” creator Michael Schur for a sun-soaked romp about archaeologists whose discovery at a Greek site spirals into an unexpected adventure. Ready to map out your watchlist? Read on for everything new on Peacock this November. New on Peacock in November 2026: Top picks 'The Uprising' This historical epic, inspired by the real events that gave rise to the legend of Robin Hood, stars Andrew Garfield as the leader of a peasant rebellion in 14th-century England. The common people combine to form a powerful force against the crown of King Richard II while war and plague ravage the country. It's an intense, action-packed thriller showcasing the uprising, backed by a stacked British cast including Jamie Bell and Tom Hollander. Stream on Peacock on November 6 'The Good Daughter' Rose Byrne and Meghann Fahy play Samantha and Charlotte Quinn, estranged sisters who’ve spent two decades trying to rebuild their lives after a night of violence forever changed their family. When a new attack hits their hometown, Charlotte, now a lawyer following in her father’s footsteps, is the first witness on the scene. The investigation that follows brings the town's long-buried secrets and painful memories back into the light. Equal parts twisty thriller and emotional family drama, it's all about the complicated bonds between sisters and family. Stream on Peacock starting November 12 'Dig' Amy Poehler reunites with “Parks and Recreation” creator Michael Schur for this new Peacock comedy. Poehler co-created and stars in “Dig,” which follows a team of archaeologists and a crew of decidedly less-dedicated college students, all spending their summer at an excavation site in Greece. When they discover a rare artifact, the whole ragtag group heads off on a huge adventure they could never have imagined. articles.title: Motorola finally puts a date on its Galaxy Ultra challenger
articles.content: TL;DR Motorola has officially confirmed that the Signature 27 will launch on November 5. The phone’s US landing page is live, showcasing its premium design and flagship hardware. A Geekbench listing reveals more performance details, but pricing remains under wraps. The original Motorola Signature had the looks and the hardware to rub shoulders with Android’s finest, but American buyers never got an invitation. Its successor is rewriting that script. It first made a cheeky appearance on Motorola’s US website, then debuted at Snapdragon Summit, putting the Galaxy Ultra and Pixel Pro on notice. Now, the Signature 27 has a date with America, and it’s just days away. Motorola has officially confirmed November 5 as the launch date for the Signature 27. In a new X teaser, the company highlights the phone’s premium design and comfortable ergonomics and invites fans to see it next Thursday.

articles.title: I used Google’s ‘Ask Maps’ feature to plan my Halloween weekend festivities — 7 events it recommended I'd actually attend
articles.content: When a holiday falls on a Friday or Saturday, I’m always overjoyed (especially if it’s my birthday). And this year, my favorite holiday just happens to be falling on a Saturday. Of course I’m talking about Halloween , which is one of an adult’s perfect excuses to get all dressed up as their favorite characters and meet up with a bunch of like-minded cosplayers (another good excuse is attending Comic-Con). I already have my costume laid out, ready to go, but there’s just one problem: I don’t have somewhere in mind that I can actually go to show off my holiday-themed wear. Then, like a sign from the heavens, I locked eyes with the Google Maps app and had a lightbulb pop up over my head. “Oh yeah! I can use the “Ask Maps” feature to find something fun to do on Halloween!” I simply tapped on the AI-powered tool inside Google Maps, asked it to find the best events I should consider going to with a few friends for Halloween and was met with a strong list of recommendations that I’m actually considering attending. Parties, a parade, a unique show and so much more (Image credit: Shutterstock) There are a few aspects of the Ask Maps feature that I appreciate. Among them is its ability to actually show the events on a local map and provide direct links to where I can get more information about them. Ask Maps’ Halloween celebration suggestions were split up into a bunch of different themes, such as Nightclubs & High-Energy Bashes, Parades, Crawls & Unique Shows, Themed Parties & Rooftop Bashes, Nightlife Cruises & Skyline Sails and Multi-Venue Crawls & Day Markets. For the first category, there were two events attached to it that caught my attention: The Haunted Asylum at CODE Astoria, Oct 31: If you want to stay closer to Queens, head over to Astoria for a full-scale haunted asylum. Expect high-energy club programming, local DJs, cocktails, and an emphasis on heavy costumes. Runs all night long from 8:00 PM to 4:00 AM. Fright Night NYC Halloween Party 2026, Oct 31: This massive Brooklyn loft party features a legendary costume competition and an infectious holiday energy. Features a massive $3,000 cash prize costume contest, making it the place to go if your friend group goes all-out on outfits. Includes complimentary rum punch during the first hour of the party from 10:00 PM to 11:00 PM. (Image credit: Shutterstock) The second event category recommended an obvious event that most folks in New York City will be popping out to. And what’s crazy is the fact that I’ve always watched it on TV but never even thought about going to and experiencing it for myself. Of course, I’m talking about my hometown’s legendary Halloween Parade. Alongside that party option, Ask Maps also brought two other amusing Halloween hangouts worth considering: New York City Village Halloween Parade, Oct 31: New York City’s absolute signature Halloween event returns for its 53rd year, packing Sixth Avenue with pure creative madness. The 2026 theme is “Body & Soul”, welcoming highly expressive and boundary-pushing costume ideas. Free to watch along the streets, or you can join the procession for free as long as your entire group is in full costume. NYC Halloween Bar Crawl 2026, Oct 31: If your group can’t decide on just one venue, this massive multi-neighborhood bar hop lets you sample the city’s fluidity. Moves seamlessly down Manhattan from a Times Square check-in point all the way into the East Village. Tickets grant access to drink specials, dance floors, and costume contests across numerous participating locations. Halloween Soirée Late Show, Oct 31: For an upscale, theatrical alternative to standard clubs, this sultry NoHo show blends dinner-theater aesthetics with holiday spirit. articles.title: I just went hands-on with the Ultrahuman Ring Pro — 7 things to know about this subscription-free Oura rival
articles.content: When Ultrahuman first announced its new flagship Ring Pro last February, we didn’t know whether the wearable would ultimately go on sale in the U.S. because of ongoing litigation with U.S.-based rival Oura. Then, in March, Ultrahuman opened preorders for the Ring Pro to U.S. customers. Now, in the final week of October, the Ultrahuman Ring Pro has officially hit U.S. store shelves at major retailers like Best Buy and Amazon for $479 . But is the Ultrahuman Ring Pro worth the hype? I’ve been wearing one for a few days — full review coming soon — and I already think it’s a seriously strong competitor to the Oura Ring 5 , the best smart ring in 2026. With that in mind, here are the seven most important things you need to know about the Ultrahuman Ring Pro. 1. It's been completely redesigned to avoid Oura's (legal) wrath (Image credit: Dan Bracaglia/Tom's Guide) The Ultrahuman Ring Pro features a unique unibody design that's purpose-built not only to withstand daily wear but also to avoid infringing on any of Oura's existing patents. As a reminder, Oura successfully litigated to keep the Ultrahuman Ring Air , the Pro's predecessor, off U.S. store shelves in 2025 for patent infringements. However, when I spoke with Mohit Kumar, the founder and CEO of Ultrahuman, earlier this year, he seemed confident in his team's reworked design for the newer model. "We went through the [U.S.] Customs procedure 177 to get the device approved, noted Kumar. " We took the right path to make sure that the design is approved by (U.S.) Customs, and they officially issue an order that says, 'This is a design which is unique and non-infringing, for the patent which Oura holds.'" Another benefit of the updated design: It features Ultrahuman's "ProRelease Technology," a safety feature that makes it relatively easy for emergency responders or medical professionals to cut the ring off for any reason (like a faulty, swollen battery ). 2. It’s pricier than the Oura Ring 5, but… (Image credit: Dan Bracaglia/Tom's Guide) The Ultrahuman Ring starts at $479 , which is $79 more than the starting cost of the Oura Ring 5 (more on that in a second). It's available in four finishes, including gold, silver, black, and titanium, with sizes ranging from five to 14. The $479 covers not only the ring but also the cost of Ultrahuman's swanky/handy Pro Charging case (further details on that too, below). 3. Core features are subscription-free (Image credit: Dan Bracaglia/Tom's Guide) Despite a higher up-front cost compared to the Oura Ring 5, the Ultrahuman Ring Pro is a better value after the first ~14 months of ownership. This is because Oura requires users to sign up for a subscription to use their smart ring for $5.99 a month or $69.99 a year. Ultrahuman, on the other hand/finger, takes a more wallet-friendly, subscription-free approach to wellness tracking, which is perhaps the most notable difference between the two brands. 4. It’s thicker and heavier than other smart rings (Image credit: Dan Bracaglia/Tom's Guide) The Ultrahuman Ring Pro is noticeably heavier than the Oura Ring 5. My size 11 silver Ultrahuman Ring Pro weighs 4.52 g versus ~2.5 g for the comparable Oura Ring 5. The latest Ultrahuman flagship is also thicker than its rival...then again, Oura's latest is one of the smallest, lightest smart rings in the world. The Ultrahuman Ring Pro has a thickness of 2.6mm around the band and ~4.8mm at the sensors, making it thicker (and heavier) than other popular smart rings I've tested/demoed, too, like the RingConn Gen 2 Air. That said, after 24 hours of wearing the Ring Pro, I hardly notice it on my left index finger, and this is coming from someone who doesn't usually rock rings. That said, let's see if my tune changes over the coming weeks. 5. Ultrahuman reworked the heart rate sensor for better accuracy (Image credit: Dan Bracaglia/Tom's Guide) In addition to a redesigned body, the Ultrahuman Ring Pro features an overhauled heart rate sensor with added processing…

articles.title: I drove the Rivian R2 for a week — and this sub-$60K electric SUV lives up to the hype
articles.content: Rivian is the EV maker to watch. It’s no coincidence that I’m seeing far more of its vehicles on the road, instantly recognizable by their distinct stadium-style halo headlights. While I came away deeply impressed with both the R1T pickup and the three-row R1S SUV , they’re simply too expensive and out of reach for most budgets. That’s why I’ve been so excited about the Rivian R2 . It represents an ambitious push to reach the masses with a much lower price tag. By trimming down its footprint compared to the full-size R1S into a practical midsize frame — while keeping its starting price under $60,000 — Rivian finally has a vehicle with mass-market appeal, and I’m all for it. After spending a full week behind the wheel of the 2027 Rivian R2 Performance, I can honestly say this eagerly awaited EV lives up to the hype and is one of the best electric cars out there. Here’s why. 2027 Rivian R2 review: Specifications John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide John Velasco / Tom's Guide 2027 Rivian R2 Performance (with Launch Edition package) Battery 87.9 kWh Motor Dual Motor (AWD) 0 to 60 mph 3.6 seconds Range 330 miles Horsepower 656 hp Wheels 22-inches MSRP $57,990 Price Tested $59,485 2027 Rivian R2 review: Testing summary (Image credit: John Velasco / Tom's Guide) I drove a total of 236.8 miles during my week testing the 2027 Rivian R2 Performance, averaging an efficiency of 3.24 mi/kWh. That's a massive leap over the dismal 1.85 mi/kWh I saw in the R1S, proving that the R2 makes the absolute most out of its 87.9 kWh battery pack. At the same time, it lands right in the efficiency sweet spot alongside premium rivals like the Audi Q6 e-tron and BMW iX xDrive45 — but with a far more attainable price tag. During long-distance drives consisting mostly of highway cruising, the Rivian R2 proved surprisingly efficient, peaking at 3.68 mi/kWh. Meanwhile, short-distance trips topped out at 3.59 mi/kWh. What makes these figures so impressive is that efficiency doesn't come at the expense of performance because the R2 still delivers all the instant punch I crave without feeling choked back to hit efficiency constraints. Home charging is another welcome step up from the R1T and R1S. Plugged into a standard 120V household outlet for Level 1 charging , it added back 29 miles of range in roughly 8.6 hours — a replenishment rate of about 3.37 mi/hr. It's also worth noting that the R2 natively uses Tesla’s NACS charging port for hassle-free access to the Supercharger network, though an included adapter still allows for seamless charging at CCS stations. 2027 Rivian R2 Performance 2027 Audi Q6 e-tron Premium quattro 2026 BMW ix xDrive45 Price tested $59,485 $77,290 88,000 Total miles driven 236.8 miles 116.8 miles…

articles.title: AWS installs an AI accelerator every 14 seconds and eyes $1 trillion annual revenue
articles.content: Amazon Web Services will become a trillion-dollar business in five to ten years, and thanks to the AI boom Amazon CEO Andy Jassy thinks it should be able to grow by 40 percent or more in 2027 or 2028. The cloud giant is already on track to generate $184 billion annual revenue this financial year, helped by 39.3 percent year-over-year growth that propelled Q3 revenue to a whisker short of $46 billion. “It’s important to remember that the vast majority of global IT spend, about 85 percent, is still on premises, and we’re in a 10- to 20-year cycle where that equation will flip to the cloud,” he said on Amazon's Q3 earnings call. “Conventional wisdom has been that linchpin workloads like mainframes or storage area networks would never move to the cloud,” he observed, before triumphantly noting “these workloads are moving.” He thinks AI will help, too. Jassy said the cloudy concern installs a new AI accelerator “about every 14 seconds, and almost as fast as we install capacity, customers are gobbling it up.” The outfit’s Bedrock AI services is already the fastest growing multi-billion dollar service in its history, Jassy said. Core compute and storage services are also soaring: the CEO said revenue from both “grew at their fastest rates in several years.” Jassy thinks the performance of Bedrock and core services are intertwined, because when users select AWS for AI workloads they want their cloudy inferencing rigs to be “near the rest of their data and apps.” The CEO said AI workloads therefore “can’t help but drive core AWS demand because AI uses core for work like reinforcement learning, post-training, and tool usage, which can’t help but drive reinvestment back into our broader AWS functionality.” He thinks this scheme is already working because margins for AI services are already “well ahead” of the figures AWS was able to achieve for its core services at a similar time in their evolution. The company expects to make $220 billion of capital expenditure in 2026 and already spent $75.9 billion last quarter alone, most of that on AWS. Jassy said the cloud colossus is finding ways to more quickly pay for its infrastructure investments. The CEO said it’s not easy to do that. “I think what we’re seeing with AI, it’s the biggest transformation in our lifetime,” he said. “Would it be more convenient if this type of acceleration and opportunity happened over 25 years and you could spread the CapEx over 25 years? Yeah, it might be more convenient, but that’s not the world that we live in, and that’s not the opportunity.” “We can fund this plan. I think it will forever change the size of Amazon. It will forever change our revenue, it will forever change our free cash flow, and we’re going to invest, and we’re going to pursue it to continue to be the significant leader like we are today.” Amazon needs AWS to land this plane, because the cloudy concern is growing much faster than the company’s retail and operations, which saw revenue rise six percent on far slimmer margins. Jassy could at least point to Prime Video becoming “a significant business with a revenue run rate in the tens of billions of dollars, [and is] now profitable in its own right.” Overall revenue was $180.17 bilion for the quarter. So if the respective growth rates of AWS and the rest of Amazon continue, in a few years we could be talking about a cloud company with a retail side hustle. ®

articles.title: Now is the perfect time for Samsung to release a cheaper Galaxy Z Fold 9 FE — and it's all because of iPhone Duo
articles.content: Foldables have been around for several years, but the recent launch of the iPhone Duo means the foldable market could be on the verge of changing in a big way. To the point where Samsung is reportedly looking to mix things up, and offer an even more diverse range of foldable-centric devices than it already does. The latest rumor claims that Samsung is currently working on a companion for the Galaxy Z Fold 9 , sharing the same wider passport-shape of the Galaxy Z Fold 8 . According to a leak on Korean network Naver , Samsung is testing two possible options, including a Galaxy Z Fold 9 Plus and a lower-priced Galaxy Z Fold 9 FE. I've already expressed some confusion as to how a Z Fold 9 Plus would sit between the Fold 9 and Fold 9 Ultra. But an FE-branded model? That's actually a very good idea, especially in the current climate. Just as long as Samsung doesn't mess things up, like it did with last year's Galaxy Z Flip 7 FE . Prices are too high right now (Image credit: Tom's Guide) It's no secret that the cost of smartphones is rising, and Samsung has been one of the worst offenders when it comes to price hikes. The Galaxy S26 series was already subjected to some price hikes at launch, depending on which version you bought, only for Samsung to raise prices again at the start of October. The Z Fold 8 Ultra was also noticeably more expensive than the Z Fold 7 , which was in turn more expensive than the Z Fold 6 . The reason for these price hikes are obvious. The cost of phone manufacturing has been rising for a number of years, and the last 12 months have seen an explosion in the cost of RAM and storage — all thanks to the current AI boom we've been experiencing. Because of that multiple electronics companies have been forced to increase prices across the board including Samsung, Apple and Google. The key problem with foldable adoption has been that they're so darn expensive, especially if you don't have easy access to Chinese brands that (usually) charge less than their international counterparts. So if you think about it, the seemingly never-ending price hikes means that now is the perfect time to start releasing lower-cost foldables. The iPhone Duo has raised a lot more awareness about foldables, and could mean higher foldable adoption rates across the board. All foldable phone makers need to do is make sure their devices are accessible, and offering something with a lower price tag is one way to do that — even if it does come with some compromises. Plus, the cost of everything is going up, and there's less money to spend on luxury purchases like new smartphones. Especially ones that cost close to $2,000. Fighting increased competition (Image credit: Tom's Guide) While the launch of the iPhone Duo will help raise awareness of foldable phones, it also means that Galaxy foldables have some serious competition — possibly for the first time ever. Apple is a popular brand, and that's reflected in the fact iPhone sales outpace any other individual phone brand. Even Samsung, easily the most popular Android brand, trailed behind Apple in global market share last year . There are plenty of people out in the world who will only ever buy an iPhone, and will never even consider the possibility of switching to a rival brand — regardless of what might be on offer. But that doesn't mean convincing people to make the switch is impossible, and this means Samsung needs something that will help fight the increased competition from Apple and convince people that a Galaxy foldable is a much better option than an iPhone Duo. Considering the Duo starts at $2,000, second only in price to the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, the obvious solution is to start offering something even cheaper. To hook into those people who saw the iPhone Duo, but were unwilling to pay quite so much money to experience what foldable phones have to offer. The Galaxy Z Fold 8 is already slightly cheaper than the Duo, especially when you can grab one on sale. But finally releasing a…

articles.title: Edge0 Releases Audio8-TTS-Realistic, a 0.6B Voice Cloning TTS Model
articles.content:
Edge0 has released Audio8-TTS-Realistic , an open-weight text-to-speech model for zero-shot voice cloning. Audio8-TTS-Realistic is a 0.6B-parameter model that clones a voice from 1 reference clip and transcript. It supports 23 languages, 12 more than its predecessor. The weights and code ship under Apache 2.0 . For developers, the catch is competitive multilingual accuracy at a size that is cheap to fine-tune and serve. TL;DR Size: 601M main-model parameters (codec excluded); up to 2,048 packed text/audio positions of context. Runs on: a CUDA GPU is recommended; smoke-tested on NVIDIA H20 in BF16. The paper reports 1.1 to 1.2 GiB peak memory on an Apple M2 CPU (INT4 ONNX). No Realistic ONNX export is public yet. Performance: ahead of larger open models on CV3, behind 4B-class models on MiniMax. Best: 4.86% average CV3 error across 9 languages, versus 7.73% for Qwen3-TTS-1.7B. Worst: 48.57% WER on Thai (CV3) and 31.35% CER on Cantonese (MiniMax). What is Audio8-TTS-Realistic? It is the second 0.6B release in Edge0’s Audio8 TTS family. It builds on Audio8-TTS-Preview-0.6b and keeps the same Transformers inference interface. The repository bundles the checkpoint, a 44.1 kHz neural audio codec, tokenizer, processor and custom code. It can also generate speech without a reference voice. New languages are Arabic, Finnish, Hindi, Indonesian, Malay, Norwegian, Portuguese, Russian, Swedish, Thai, Turkish and Vietnamese. How does the architecture work? The model uses a dual-autoregressive (DualAR) design inspired by Fish Audio S2 Pro . According to the technical research report , the slow branch is built on Qwen2.5 0.5B. It has 24 layers at width 896 and runs at about 21.5 frames per second. Each step predicts text tokens plus the first audio codebook. A shallow 4-layer fast branch then predicts the remaining 9 codebooks in parallel. Sequential compute therefore happens only at the frame level. How does Edge0 train for realism? The team argues that word error rate (WER) and speaker similarity (SIM) miss rhythm, pauses and timing. A model can score well on both and still sound synthetic. Training runs in 3 stages: Multilingual supervised fine-tuning (SFT). GRPO with a combined reward: 0.7 weight on WER, 0.3 on SIM. GRPO guided by a learned realism critic. The critic scores each output against a matched human recording of the same sentence. It was trained on a quality ladder built from 6 open-source TTS systems. These were ranked in a private blind listening study, with human recordings at the top. Synthetic pause compression adds finer rungs to the ladder. An identity-erasure loss stops the critic from rewarding generator fingerprints. The critic head has about 3M parameters on top of a frozen WavLM-large encoder. A duration penalty also kicks in beyond 1.35x the reference length. This blocks the policy from gaming the critic with slower speech. The final stage used only Chinese and English prompts. It still improved both aggregate metrics on the 13 lower-resource languages. Their error fell from 22.53% to 20.77%, and SIM rose from 0.637 to 0.679. Step through

The realism stage used only Chinese and English prompts, yet improved both metrics on the 13 additional languages. Source: technical report, Table 1.

articles.title: Can boiling water cause damage to your pipes? My plumber husband reveals his expert tips
articles.content: I'll be honest, despite living with a plumber, there's still plenty of things I do wrong when it comes to the pipes in my home. And while my husband's more than happy to tell me why I need to stop clogging the bathtub drain with my hair, there are some things we never discuss. When someone recently asked me whether it was safe to pour boiling water down the sink, I didn't know what to say. So, I turned to my husband, just as I did when I wanted to know how often you should actually clean your shower head ? It turns out when it comes to pouring boiling water down your drains, most of the time it's no problem at all. In fact, sometimes it can actually be helpful. But, there's still some instances when you need to be more careful. Here's my plumber husband's top tips. Is it safe to pour boiling water down your sink? (Image credit: Shutterstock) My plumber husband's first response was to simply say: "Yes, it's not a problem." With most home pipes, exposure to boiling water won't cause any issues. But, when I poked him for some extra advice, he added: "It's not going to damage anything and it could potentially clear minor blockages. "It's actually probably something you want to start with if you think you've got a blockage, before you move onto using chemicals or anything more potent," he explains. But, there are still some instances, he warned, that can cause your pipes to suffer from long-term exposure to boiling water. When is it not safe to pour boiling water down your sink? (Image credit: Shutterstock) While a lot of households have metal pipes, there are still a proportion that don't (especially newer builds). "If you have plastic or PVC pipes, you should be more cautious. There's potential for the hot water to melt or misshape your pipes with excessive exposure," he reveals. Though, he was quick to add that excessive exposure means doing it a heck of a lot , which he doesn't believe anyone would be doing. Simply pouring away the remains of a kettle or draining your pasta water won't have devastating effects to your pipes, but if you're inclined to do it regularly than you may be causing an issue. While you may want to grab your drain clog remover when you notice your sink backing up, it might still be worth pouring some boiling water down the sink as your first port of call. If that doesn't budget it, you can try a solution like Drano's Max Gel Drain Clog Remover and allow it to sit for 15-30 minutes before flushing with hot tap water. View Deal Does running cold water at the same time help? (Image credit: Shutterstock) You might have heard of a 'hack' that some people suggest where you run cold water from your tap at the same time as pouring the boiling water down the sink to lower the temperature. And while my husband plumber suggests it would cool it down, he adds: "It'd just be like running the hot water tap, only you do run a small risk of thermal shock. I'm not sure what would be the benefit. All you're doing is cooling down the water, but it wouldn't be causing an issue in the first place." He suggests that if you're looking to protect your pipes, you shouldn't be wary of boiling water. Instead, you should be focusing on not washing down any grease, fats or food waste into your sink as that could cause blockages that are a lot harder to solve. articles.title: In the year AI re-wrote the infosec rulebook, it’s comforting to know crypto exchanges still have bad security
articles.content: Crypto exchange Binance has paused trading after discovering unknown parties cracked one of its workers’ laptops and used it to make massive trades Late on Thursday, US time, the company used its social media feeds to report “Our teams are aware of reports of a potential security issue and are actively investigating.” The exchange insisted “User funds are completely safe” and warned its customers “should remain cautious of scams and should not trust unofficial links, messages, or requests for account information.” The company soon froze $2.5 billion worth of assets and warned that the figure could go higher “as our teams work closely with law enforcement, issuers, blockchain intelligence firms and industry partners to trace and freeze additional assets.” To prevent the matter worsening, Binance halted all trading, deposits, and withdrawals. It also promised to cover any losses. About an hour ago at the time of writing, Binance posted an update on the incident that explains what it thinks went wrong. “Binance's initial investigation suggests that the security incident may involve a compromised DevOps engineer’s laptop, which allowed an attacker to gain access to a service container and submit unauthorized withdrawal transactions,” the post states. The company also hiked the amount it thinks is at risk to $6.3 billion and repeated its promise to cover any customer losses. The update also says Binance found no evidence of any wallet private key leak, suggesting that customers’ holdings remain secure. When they can use them again, as Binance is yet to resume trading. Binance hasn’t explained how attackers gained access to the engineer’s laptop. The scant details provided make it hard to rule out a successful phishing attack, or perhaps a supply chain attack on a package the developer used. Binance says it will spill once it knows exactly what happened. Cryptocurrency outfits have a long and inglorious history of falling victim to cyberattacks, perhaps starting with the 2011 raid on Mt Gox , to incidents allegedly perpetrated by nation-states , and, just last week, another situation possibly involving an AI-powered attacker . ®

articles.title: Security experts warn North Korean hackers aren't just using AI in their new campaigns, but also 'post-quantum' encryption
articles.content: Kaspersky says Lazarus's Operation FlashHole, active since at least July 2025, hit at least three South Korean software, construction, and telecom equipment firms An updated LPEClient tool uses four ML-KEM-1024 key exchanges to protect payload delivery, a design Check Point also documented The post-quantum layer guards traffic against future decryption, not endpoint detection, and the most likely way in for the hackers was still phishing North Korea's most notorious hacking group has been caught protecting its malware with the same post-quantum cryptography that governments and tech firms are still rolling out to safeguard their own data. In its analysis of a campaign dubbed Operation FlashHole , Kaspersky's Global Research and Analysis Team (GReAT) says an updated version of LPEClient, a Lazarus Group tool, now uses ML-KEM-1024, a key exchange mechanism designed to resist attacks from future quantum computers, to secure the channel it uses to download more malware. The findings describe a campaign active since at least July 2025 that has hit at least three South Korean organizations in the software, construction, and wired communication equipment manufacturing sectors. A fake AI-tailored résumé, a mandatory plugin, and quantum-resistant encryption The way in was familiar: Kaspersky found a GitHub Pages site tied to a GitHub account, created in September 2025, that the attackers used for command and control. The site first showed the résumé of a supposed senior network appliance developer, likely seen by an employee of the communications equipment maker, before the attackers swapped it in January 2026for an interior design showcase that probably targeted the construction firm. Kaspersky assesses with medium-to-high confidence that targets received spear-phishing emails linking to these sites, which loaded JavaScript from attacker-controlled domains, though it could not determine exactly what triggered the infection. From there, the chain ran through INISAFE CrossWeb EX, financial security software South Koreans need in order to use many online banking and government websites. How it was abused is unclear, but the malware ended up running in memory with elevated privileges, spawned by a CrossWeb EX build released in 2023 after a public advisory from South Korea's KrCERT. That is a well-trodden route; Kaspersky says Lazarus abused CrossWeb EX in 2021, 2022, and 2023, and in Operation SyncHole , disclosed in April 2025, it used Cross EX, a related program, to compromise at least six organizations, and we also reported on the group exploiting a zero-day in MagicLine4NX , another South Korean authentication tool. Kaspersky believes the photo on the résumé site was AI-generated, citing missing EXIF metadata and an unnatural texture, and that AI most likely built the site too, given a candidate name resembling Korea's equivalent of "John Doe" and a portfolio stuffed with filler details and unrelated companies. ojun Ryu, senior security researcher at Kaspersky GReAT, said the findings suggest Lazarus is "bringing AI into its long-established playbook," a shift Kaspersky has also seen among other Lazarus-aligned groups. That fits a broader pattern, from Kimsuky using ChatGPT to forge a South Korean military ID to North Korean IT workers using generative AI to get hired at Western firms . The more striking change is inside LPEClient, a profiling and payload delivery tool that first appeared in 2019. The new version no longer stores its own server address; instead, it relays traffic through ClientHub, a newly discovered loader with a variant that talks to its operators via Dropbox. It profiles installed security products and the Windows patch level, now also checks whether protections such as Shadow Stack are enabled, and encrypts that report with GOST, Russia's national cipher standard. articles.content: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Android 16 is now the most widely used Android version, accounting for 25.4% of active devices, up from 7.5% in December 2025. Android 17 has reached just 1% adoption, despite becoming available in June 2026, and even Android 8.1 has a larger share. Android fragmentation remains a problem, with 43.6% of active devices still running Android 13 or older. Android 16 has finally become the most widely used version of Google’s mobile operating system, but the latest Android distribution figures suggest that getting users onto newer software remains a challenge.

articles.title: PC chip plunge wipes out a quarter of Intel’s value
articles.content: Intel’s share price sank by almost a quarter on Thursday after the company revealed a deep dip in sales of PC processors. The rout began after the silicon-slinger posted Q3 results that included some nice numbers, such as a 21 percent year on year revenue jump to $16.5 billion, helped by 78 percent growth for datacenter and AI products, and gross margins of 43 percent. The revenue number was at the high end of Intel’s revenue guidance of $15.8-16.8 billion, and the gross margin beat its predictions by two points. Outweighing those upsides was a decline in revenue for client computing and physical AI products, which saw incoming cash reach $8.1 billion but fall five percent year-over-year and nine percent decline from last quarter. In prepared remarks [PDF] published to coincide with Intel’s earnings announcement, CEO Lip Bu Tan said “In recent weeks, our customers began signaling a PC slowdown based on memory prices and availability. Year-to-date system end-point prices have increased significantly placing additional pressure on already limited IT budgets.” “The pace of the PC correction has accelerated over the last two months, as our OEM partners are aggressively managing inventory to match the softer sell through,” he added, before predicting that the market for PC chips will shrink by 12 percent next year and remain tough “until memory availability and prices begin to normalize.” Which may not be for years, given Korean memory-maker SK Hynix this week predicted that memory shortages will persist until the year 2030. Intel’s biggest business is therefore in trouble. AI and Xeons riding to a rocky rescue Tan tried to give investors reasons to be cheerful, by saying Intel sees a “resurgence in demand for CPU” sparked by customers’ desire for computing systems that consume less energy. “Increasingly, energy efficiency is becoming the most important metric for the AI infrastructure build-out,” he said. That matters, Tan argued, because “While GPUs are great at ‘thinking tasks,’ deterministic CPUs are far more efficient at ‘finding’ tasks. While a GPU reasoning query can run as high as multiple watt-hours of energy, a single CPU-based query could cost only joules of energy.” The CEO reasoned that lower energy consumption is important in the context of agentic AI – the idea that we will all soon run many autonomous agents to handle personal and professional scutwork. “Applying even conservative estimates to the total number of digital agents, and agents serviced per CPU, it is easy to anticipate a massive dollar and unit TAM [total addressable market] for CPUs over the coming five years,” Tan said. “By our estimates, server CPU TAM, largely driven by agentic workloads, could increase as much as 5X from where it is today, from $40B to more than $200B over five years.” But during its earnings call, Intel execs admitted it may struggle to cash in on that boom in the short and longer term as the company struggles to source key supplies like silicon wafers. Asked if Intel can meet demand for server CPUs and if investors should therefore expect further growth in datacenter product sales early in Intel’s next financial year, chief financial officer Dave Zinsner declined to offer any guidance. “There is going to be a strong driver of demand for CPUs,” he demurred. “We see that continuing all through next year. We are working on the supply side of the equation to make sure that we can meet what customers need. We will likely not fully meet what they require, but I think we are going to be in a more challenging situation in the first half of the year than we are in the second half.” Intel is trying to shift production around its fleet of fabs so it can crank out as much silicon as possible and will even devote some PC chip production capacity to datacenter products. But overall, Chipzilla is clearly in a spot of bother. CEO Lip Bu Tan said his plan to “rebuild” Intel will be “a multiyear journey” and insisted “We have made enormous…

articles.title: Fox News’ pro-data center coverage explodes 420% following GOP warning that Democrats are defeating Republicans
articles.content: Fox News pro-data center perspectives increased fivefold following a warning from the National Republican Senatorial Committee Republicans are losing the midterm electoral race in Ohio, and data centers are central to the Democrat campaign Tech companies were told to "fix how Ohioans see" data centers New research has found that Fox News coverage on pro-data center topics has risen by 420% since August 18 2026 - the day the National Republican Senatorial Committee warned tech companies that Republican candidates were losing to Democrats in key battleground states. These are the findings of Media Matters , a nonprofit journalism watchdog which analyzed the two weeks preceding the GOP warning and compared it to the following period. Pro-data center perspectives from guests and Fox News hosts quintupled. AI, and the data centers that power the technology, have become a hot button issue in the run up to the November US midterm elections. Numerous polls have suggested that the majority of Americans oppose the buildout of AI data centers and infrastructure. AI opposition is a Chinese psyop The private memo from the GOP, as reported by Axios , explained that tech companies need to change public perspectives on AI data centers, lest Republicans candidates lose to a “Democrat candidate who wants to stop data center construction altogether, which will cause America to lose the AI race to China”. In Ohio, the campaign of Democratic nominee Sherrod Brown is being driven by anti-data center sentiment, which the GOP fears could cost Republican incumbent Jon Husted his seat. The GOP called Brown’s strategy “significantly more effective than traditional messaging tracts.” To that end, the GOP urged tech companies to shift perspectives on to “who benefits, who pays, and why a community should want one.” Comparing the number of claims made before and after the GOP memo, the researchers found that claims in favor of data centers jumped from 39 in a two week period to 203 in the following two weeks. The balance of claims in favor and against data centers was also skewed, with those favorable to data centers outnumbering those against by almost double. Around 56% of the claims made argued that AI data centers were essential to the US’ progress and prosperity, with 43% of claims arguing that the widespread opposition to AI data centers is being fueled by bad actors such as “far-left activists” and the Chinese government. Fox News has frequently painted data centers as a boon to regions with large concentrations, with Fox News’ Will Cain pulling upon examples of Virginia’s Loudoun County as “data center alley, the richest county in America.” Research has found that opposition to data centers is not a politically partisan issue , with the majority of opposition coming from working class communities irrespective of Democrat or Republican leaning.

articles.title: The US Air Force wants to use AI to help with its mid-air refuelling problems
articles.content: US Air Force wants AI to detect mistakes during aerial refuelling Tanker cameras would supply footage for automated analysis of refuelling operations AI would monitor aircraft speed, alignment, positioning, and approach velocity The US Air Force is exploring using AI to identify mistakes during aerial refuelling operations and improve how crews receive performance feedback. The proposed system would analyze footage captured by tanker aircraft cameras, identifying flight manoeuvres and operational errors that conventional assessments might overlook. Military officials want the technology to provide detailed evaluations of refuelling exercises, reducing dependence on human judgement during one of aviation's most demanding procedures. AI system will monitor aircraft movements and refuelling accuracy The initiative focuses on developing software capable of examining interactions between tanker aircraft and approaching receivers throughout the complicated fuel transfer process. Using computer vision and machine learning, the technology would examine aircraft movements and determine whether crews maintained appropriate separation and alignment. It would also monitor the refuelling boom, comparing its movements against aircraft trajectories to identify potentially dangerous deviations during fuel delivery. Measurements would include aircraft speed, relative positioning, approach velocity and alignment, allowing instructors to examine specific manoeuvres rather than relying on general observations. The proposed software would automatically identify departures from expected flight conditions and generate performance information for instructors reviewing completed refuelling missions. Currently, assessments depend substantially on instructor observations, crew evaluations and manually examining recorded footage, according to the military's research solicitation. These methods can produce inconsistent judgements, particularly when instructors interpret the same manoeuvre differently or overlook brief errors during complicated operations. Therefore, the software’s assessment will include graphical overlays, colour-coded performance maps and chronological displays identifying significant events during individual refuelling exercises. The Air Force consequently wants automated measurements that could provide more consistent evaluations while helping personnel understand precisely where mistakes occurred. The project falls under the Small Business Innovation Research programme, which invites companies to develop technological solutions addressing specific military requirements. Interested developers have until November 25 2026 to submit applications outlining how their proposed systems could satisfy the service's operational and training requirements. KC-46 tanker technology and future training applications The initial development effort concentrates on the KC-46 Pegasus, a refuelling aircraft equipped with cameras supporting remotely controlled fuel transfer operations. Its remote vision equipment allows boom operators to guide the refuelling apparatus using camera feeds and 3D displays instead of direct observation. However, the aircraft's existing viewing technology has experienced persistent technical difficulties, although military officials expect most outstanding problems to be resolved soon. Developers are expected to consider interactive review environments that allow pilots and instructors to examine manoeuvres from different perspectives. The technology could eventually connect with flight simulators, virtual reality equipment and augmented reality training platforms already used for aviation instruction. Military planners want an operational prototype suitable for integration with existing training arrangements for at least one category of receiving aircraft. The solicitation also identifies potential applications beyond refuelling, including automated assessments of other aviation activities throughout the Department of Defense…

articles.title: Andy Jassy’s prediction: Amazon could have two $1 trillion businesses within a decade
articles.content: Amazon CEO Andy Jassy told analysts Thursday that “some folks are sleeping a bit” on how much progress the company’s stores business has made. (GeekWire File Photo) No company has ever had a business with $1 trillion in annual revenue. Andy Jassy says Amazon is on a path to have two. Amazon Web Services and the company’s stores business could both reach that milestone in the next five to 10 years, the Amazon CEO said Thursday in the company’s third-quarter earnings release and on its call with analysts. It’s “pretty rare” for Jassy to make a projection that far out, Morgan Stanley analyst Brian Nowak observed on the call, asking how he gets there. Related AWS growth hits 39%, its fastest in nearly five years, as Amazon misses on earnings Jassy’s answer started with AWS, which is at a $184 billion annual revenue run rate after growing 39% in the third quarter. He expects growth of more than 40% in both 2027 and 2028, and pointed to a $578 billion backlog of contracted AWS revenue. The largest customers reserve capacity in huge blocks, sometimes as much as a gigawatt at a time, giving Amazon “very good visibility” into 2027, 2028 and part of 2029, he said. Beyond that, he said, businesses are still early in using AI, the cost of running AI models keeps falling, and new uses keep emerging, such as AI models finding and fixing security flaws. “You can’t predict with any certainty five to 10 years from now, especially at these types of growth rates,” Jassy said of AWS. “But it’s not a stretch for us to imagine that this could be over a trillion dollar business.” Jassy’s forecast is a big jump from seven months ago. In March, Jassy told employees that AWS had a chance to reach at least $600 billion in annual revenue within about a decade, double his earlier expectation, according to Reuters . Amazon’s stores business is bigger than AWS. Sales from Amazon’s online and physical stores totaled $309 billion over the past 12 months, or about $575 billion if Jassy is including third-party seller services and advertising in his trillion-dollar projection. We’ve asked Amazon to clarify. For comparison, Walmart, the world’s largest retailer, had $713 billion in revenue in its most recent fiscal year. Whichever numbers he’s using, Jassy said “some folks are sleeping a bit” on how much progress the stores business has made. Jassy argued that Amazon’s stores business is gaining ground on competitors. Amazon added more than $90 billion in gross sales over the past 12 months, he said, and is adding about twice as much per quarter as its next-largest U.S. competitor. Units sold are up nearly 15% so far this year, Jassy said. He noted that nearly 80% of retail sales still happen in physical stores, which he expects to shift online over time. The bold prediction came on a rough day for the company. Amazon shares fell about 6% in after-hours trading after its profit fell short of Wall Street’s expectations . It’s not going to be cheap to get there. Amazon expects to spend about $220 billion on capital projects this year, mostly for AWS, and Jassy said the company will spend “meaningfully more” in 2027. He said Amazon has “a clear line of sight to attractive financial returns” and is earning back its capital spending faster than before. The impact is showing up in Amazon’s finances. Its free cash flow, the cash left over after capital spending, was negative $42.4 billion over the past 12 months, compared with positive $14.8 billion a year earlier. With its spending running ahead of the cash its businesses bring in, Amazon has raised $115 billion through long-term debt this year. Its interest expense more than tripled in the third quarter to $1.7 billion, cutting into its profit. “We’re in the very early days of this inflection,” Jassy said. “Our strategy is working, and I expect it will for the foreseeable future.”
